subject: BlueRiver pilot: MAP, gating criteria, and pass/fail protocol
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tim Jenkins <tim.jenkins@blueriverhealth.com>, Asha Rao <asha.rao@blueriverhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: BlueRiver pilot: MAP, gating criteria, and pass/fail protocol

Tim / Asha —

Thanks for the conversation earlier. As promised, attached is a first-pass mutual action plan (BlueRiver_MAP_v1.xlsx) and a concise pass/fail protocol we can use during the 6-week pilot. Below is the high-level flow and the acceptance signals we need to gate to close. Please review and call out any must-haves from your side so we can lock dates.

Key milestones (proposed)
- Week 0 (Nov 29–Dec 3): Kickoff, SSO test account, data access & ingestion (sample dataset only)
- Week 1–2: Integration & baseline runs (inference with our hosted endpoint, opt quantized model)
- Week 3: Eval run 1 — prompt-suite (attached), functional correctness sampling, latency profiling
- Week 4: Optimizations & second-run validation (cache tuning, batching profiles)
- Week 5: Final validation & handoff to BlueRiver infra team for integration tests
- Week 6: Sign-off window and backstop for remediation/extension

Exit gates / pass-fail signals (high level)
- Latency: p95 generation latency <= 350ms for 75-token prompts in controlled baseline (see SLA_latency_diagram.png)
- Throughput: Sustained 120 reqs/min for the demo workload without errors above 1%
- Quality: BLEU-style scoring not ideal for this domain — we'll use a failure-rate threshold on the prompt-suite where <5% of prompts produce hallucinations or broken formatted outputs (we'll provide examples in the prompt-suite)
- Security/compliance: SSO (SAML) login validated and data retention headers set to 30 days for pilot artifacts
- Data handling: No patient PHI to be transmitted; only de-identified records as agreed in the NDA

Acceptance tests (owners in parentheses)
- Integration sanity (Redwood infra / BlueRiver dev): end-to-end call with sample payload (Dev Patel)
- Latency & throughput sweep (Redwood SRE): load profile run with 3 seed model variants (Ben Carter)
- Functional correctness (Joint): run prompt-suite and adjudicate failures (Monica + BlueRiver SME)
- Failover & fallback test (Marissa Cole/internal CS): induce a model-fallback and verify graceful degradation

Open asks for BlueRiver:
- Confirm SSO test user by end of day Thursday (Nov 26)
- Confirm whether retention must be 14 or 30 days (legal/infra)
- Identify the SME(s) who will adjudicate prompt failures during week 3

I've attached the draft MAP and the example prompt-suite that we'll run in week 3. If this looks good I'm happy to push the MAP into HubSpot and generate a shared checklist so we can track owners against each action.

Thanks — talk soon,

Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0189

Attachments: BlueRiver_MAP_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), example-prompt-suite.csv (csv), SLA_latency_diagram.png (png)
From: Tim Jenkins <tim.jenkins@blueriverhealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Asha Rao <asha.rao@blueriverhealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: BlueRiver pilot: MAP, gating criteria, and pass/fail protocol

Monica —

Thanks for the clear plan. A few quick clarifications from our side:

1) Latency target — the 350ms p95 is reasonable for the demo, but for clinical workflow integration we may need a tighter goal (<=250ms p95). Can you call out which model & config corresponds to 350ms so we know the delta?
2) Data retention — legal prefers 14 days for pilot artifacts unless we can guarantee field-level redaction. We'll confirm by EOD Friday.
3) Adjudication — I will be the primary SME, Asha will assist. We also want an export of raw examples that failed so we can attach to JIRA tickets.

Also: is there a fallback plan if the throughput test reveals a model-level bottleneck? We'd like to know the options (reduce context length, lighter quant, route to a lower-cost instance) and the approximate time to pivot.

Tim
Director of Clinical Platforms
BlueRiver Health

Subject: RE: BlueRiver pilot: MAP, gating criteria, and pass/fail protocol

Monica — quick internal note before we lock back to BlueRiver.

Technical notes and recommended adjustments:
- The 350ms p95 baseline in the diagram assumes the quantized medium model (8-bit) and a batch size of 4 with continuous batching enabled. If BlueRiver needs 250ms p95 we should plan to run the same tests on the smaller distilled variant (expected ~220–270ms p95) and validate for quality delta. Dev can prep the model variants.
- Throughput: sustained 120 reqs/min should be fine on our dedicated dev pool, but error rate could spike if prompt length varies widely — propose we lock to a 75-token standard for the pilot load test; we'll add a note to the MAP.
- Pass/fail adjudication: propose a lightweight triage sheet (shared Google Sheet) where BlueRiver flags failures and we mark root cause (prompt, model, infra). Marissa can run the fallthrough test for fallback verification.

Owner matrix (short):
- Provision SSO test user (BlueRiver) — owner: Tim/Asha, due: Nov 26
- Model variant run & latency sweep — owner: Dev Patel, due: Dec 3
- Prompt-suite run & adjudication — owner: Monica + Tim, due: Dec 10
- Final sign-off doc & acceptance — owner: Monica, due: Dec 17

Ben
Principal SRE | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

Subject: BlueRiver pilot: Updated MAP, test matrix, and decision checklist (please sign)

Tim / Asha —

Attached is an update addressing the questions above: BlueRiver_MAP_v1.xlsx (updated v1.1), plus an exported prompt-suite with the pass/fail examples. TL;DR on changes:

- Added explicit model-variant mapping to each latency target (sheet: model-mapping). 350ms p95 = quantized medium; 250ms p95 path = distilled-small (we'll run both and document quality delta).
- Retention set to 14 days for pilot artifacts per your legal preference (adjustable if needed).
- Added a fallback decision tree: first attempt is quantization/packaged lighter model (less than 24 hours turnaround), second is dynamic routing to a lower-latency regional pool (72 hours if infra changes required).
- Included an explicit acceptance checklist (sheet: acceptance-checklist) with binary pass/fail rows so sign-off is quick.

Immediate asks to keep timeline: please approve the checklist rows below by reply (yes/no) and confirm the SME names. Once we have that I will: 1) create the checklist in HubSpot, 2) send DocuSign for the MAP signature, and 3) schedule the kickoff.

Acceptance checklist (please reply yes/no)
- SSO test user provisioned by Nov 26 — yes/no
- Retention: 14 days — yes/no
- SME for adjudication: Tim Jenkins — yes/no
- Run throughput sweep on 75-token standard — yes/no
- Sign-off on final acceptance window (Dec 17–Dec 23) — yes/no

If we get responses today/tomorrow I can keep the current proposed kickoff date (Nov 29). If you need to shift any item I can push the map and adjust dates.

Thanks again — attaching the updated docs and a single-line summary we can drop into the PO/Statement-of-Work.

Best,
Monica Patel
